**8B.8 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

**Bottom line:** Mostly no. I found limited evidence of tactical adaptation in macro policy and a few administrative sectors, but the main 2024 crisis response was coercive, blame-shifting, and ultimately failed. I did not find strong evidence of a broad mid-year course correction or a systematic replacement of ineffective implementers before collapse.

**Positive / partial evidence**
- **Bangladesh IMF review says corrective macro steps were underway** | IMF | June 24, 2024 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf | Claim: Bangladesh had already realigned the exchange rate, adopted a crawling peg, tightened monetary policy, and advanced tax/subsidy reforms; IMF said program performance was broadly on track. Summary: strongest evidence of course-correction under external pressure. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Bangladesh makes e-procurement mandatory** | Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | March 6, 2024 | https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html | Claim: online procurement was made mandatory, with broad agency registration and improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. Summary: real administrative correction that reduces discretion and can replace informal, ineffective contracting practices. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Health ministry launches evidence-based medical education strategy** | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh | Claim: the strategy was built on workforce studies and a technical working group to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. Summary: shows evidence-based adjustment inside a sector ministry. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **WHO peer review identifies gaps and priority actions** | WHO | July 11, 2024 | https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn | Claim: Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. Summary: concrete measurement-and-correction mechanism, though narrow and technical. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Cabinet mixes a few technocrats with loyalists** | BSS | January 11, 2024 | https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551 | Claim: Hasina formed a 37-member cabinet that included two technocrats, Yeafesh Osman and Samanta Lal Sen. Summary: weak positive evidence that she did not rely only on party operatives, but the cabinet remained mostly Awami League-centered. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Rohingya repatriation pursued through China-mediated talks** | TBS News / UNB | July 10, 2024 | https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar | Claim: Hasina pushed a diplomatic track for Rohingya repatriation through talks with Myanmar and support from China. Summary: limited evidence of method adaptation in a security-adjacent issue. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Nuclear safety framed through safeguards and IAEA support** | Dhaka Tribune | April 30, 2024 | https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear-non-proliferation-peaceful-use | Claim: Bangladesh said it would maintain transparency, safety, and security for nuclear plants and highlighted IAEA training and safeguards. Summary: narrow but real evidence of institutional correction in a high-risk domain. **QIDs:** 8B.8

**Negative / stronger evidence**
- **Hasina refused a neutral authority for the election** | Reuters | January 4, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/ | Claim: the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. Summary: suggests she did not adapt by loosening control over the political apparatus when legitimacy was already weak. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **July crackdown escalated instead of correcting course** | Reuters | July 20, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/ | Claim: Reuters described soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns as protests escalated. Summary: this is coercive escalation, not tactical correction. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Hasina kept curfew in place and blamed opponents** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153 | Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. Summary: strong evidence of blame-shifting and refusal to pivot toward de-escalation. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **UN says the crackdown killed more than 170 and blackout increased impunity** | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights | Claim: more than 170 people were killed and internet shutdowns increased impunity. Summary: evidence that the government’s response worsened the situation rather than correcting it. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **HRW says the July crackdown was the deadliest in recent Bangladesh history** | Human Rights Watch | August 26, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses | Claim: the crackdown killed at least 440 people, with excessive force by law enforcement and Awami League-linked youth violence. Summary: strong evidence that Hasina did not restrain or replace abusive implementers in time. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Army refusal to fire shows coercive plan failed, not that Hasina corrected course** | Reuters | August 7, 2024 | https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html | Claim: the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. Summary: indicates her coercive tactic failed because implementers would not fully comply; I found no evidence she then replaced them or pivoted meaningfully. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Macro deterioration persisted despite reforms** | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1 | Claim: widening current-account deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, IMF dependence, and stagnant private-sector job creation persisted. Summary: the corrective macro agenda did not clearly produce an improved trajectory in 2024. **QIDs:** 8B.8
- **Crony capitalism and elite capture remained the governing pattern** | The Daily Star | October 31, 2024 | https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796 | Claim: a white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. Summary: strong evidence against replacing ineffective or patronage-based implementers with clean professional managers. **QIDs:** 8B.8

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong contemporaneous source showing Hasina conducted a broad cabinet or security-sector purge in response to failed tactics during the July crisis.
- The best positive items are mostly sector-specific, technically narrow, or driven by external pressure/partner financing.
- The clearest accountability signals I found after the crisis were post-ouster probes and inquiries, which do not show in-office self-correction.

**Overall assessment for 8B.8:** weak-to-moderate evidence of limited adaptation in macro/technical domains, but stronger evidence that Hasina did not meaningfully change methods, replace failed implementers, or redirect the crisis response when core tactics were failing.
